ideas.title: A puddle of sky came down
ideas.critique: This is round 1's sky mirror, shrunk to a low sheet that drifts over the meadow while friends react to it. That drifting-patch-plus-reaction shape is the grey-draft patch again, and shouts making rings echo the speech-becomes-matter run. What is strong is that a low, close mirror fixes the old risk: upside-down friends you can actually read, wobbling in a rippling conductor, is an image only the tracer can make. It falls flat if the ripples are faint or the reflection is blurry.

ideas.title: The sun comes down for a walk
ideas.critique: A wandering light that friends chase or fetch is the moth and round 1's moon cannon again, and flowers turning or a dog fetching it are the expected gags. What is strong is that the island loses its sky light and its only light walks around, with shadows swinging around everything. That changes how the whole island looks and is a real lighting stunt, but only if the dark is truly dark and the shadow sweep is the star of the film.

ideas.title: Midnight, everyone swaps
ideas.critique: This is round 1's Lumi-in-Gloop body swap spread to everyone, and minds meeting their old bodies is the same reaction beat as a friend gasping at its own ghost in Yesterday. A rule that breaks the link between name, voice and body for the whole island is truly radical. But in a film, wrong gaits and moved name tags easily read as random glitches, so the swap has to be legible in the first seconds or it becomes a confused-friends gag reel.
